stories.headline: India Ready To Extend "Any Help" To End Russia-Ukraine War: S Jaishankar
stories.title: India Ready To Extend "Any Help" To End Russia-Ukraine War: S Jaishankar
stories.summary: "India has consistently maintained that this is not an era of war", S Jaishankar said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Jaishankar arrived in Kyiv amid intensified fighting between Russia and Ukraine and said the visit had both bilateral and broader significance.

Kyiv: India is willing to extend "any help in any manner" to facilitate an end to the Ukraine-Russia war, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Thursday during wide-ranging discussions with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv.
Speaking at a joint press statement with Sybiha after their meeting, Jaishankar reiterated India's long-standing position that the conflict cannot be resolved on the battlefield.
"India has consistently maintained that this is not an era of war, and that solutions will not emerge from the battlefield," he said.

Jaishankar referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek two days ago on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, where Modi called for an end to the prolonged conflict.
"Every passing day of conflict only means more deaths and more destruction.
Understandably, it is for the parties involved to find a way.
But if India can be of any help in any manner, we are ready," he said.
India has repeatedly advocated dialogue and diplomacy as the way forward to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
"In consonance with Prime Minister Modi's call for an end to war, my visit has a focus on the prospects of dialogue and diplomacy.
I will be taking back the views and positions shared today by the Ukrainian side," he added.
Later, Jaishankar called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and briefed him on his discussions with Sybiha, including ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.

stories.headline: Heavy rain wreaks havoc across states; 5 dead in UP, flood threat rises in Bihar, Bengal
stories.title: Heavy rain wreaks havoc across states; 5 dead in UP, flood threat rises in Bihar, Bengal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Train services were disrupted in West Bengal, while landslides and road closures affected transport and water supply in Himachal Pradesh.

New Delhi: Heavy rain disrupted normal life across several states on Thursday, leaving five people dead in Uttar Pradesh, pushing the Ganga towards its “highest flood mark” in Bihar and triggering landslides, road blockages and train disruptions in other parts of the country.
Five people, including three members of a family, died in separate rain-related incidents in Chitrakoot, Amethi and Barabanki districts, officials said.
In Chitrakoot, a mud house collapsed in Barachhi village, killing a 32-year-old man and his two children, aged five and one.
His wife and daughter were injured in the incident.
A 66-year-old man died after a mud wall collapsed in Naya Purwa village in Amethi on Wednesday evening.
In Barabanki, a 62-year-old man was killed and his son-in-law injured when a mud wall collapsed on them in Dhanouli village late Wednesday night.
Barabanki is among 23 districts in Uttar Pradesh currently affected by floods.
In Bihar, authorities stepped up vigilance as the Ganga continued to rise.
The river is expected to cross its “highest flood mark” at Patna's Gandhi Ghat on Thursday night, according to the Disaster Management Department.
Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inspected the rising water level along JP Ganga Path and directed officials to take steps to ensure public safety.

Residents in riverbank and low-lying areas of Bhojpur, Patna, Saran, Vaishali, Nalanda, Begusarai, Lakhisarai and Jehanabad were advised to remain alert and avoid unnecessary movement near ghats and embankments.

stories.headline: Flood relief in Pathanamthitta to be disbursed from September 5
stories.title: Flood relief in Pathanamthitta to be disbursed from September 5
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The ₹10,000 financial assistance announced for families and commercial establishments affected by the August 1 floods in Pathanamthitta district will be disbursed from September 5, Revenue Minister.
A.P. Anil Kumar said on Thursday.
The assurance comes amid reports that the promised assistance had not reached any of the flood-affected families in the State weeks after its announcement.
Presiding over a Revenue Department review meeting at the Collectorate, the Minister said the government would ensure that the assistance reached the beneficiaries at the earliest.
The amount will be released to families and business establishments for which the assessment of flood-related damage has been completed, the Minister said.
The government’s policy was to ensure that relief reached affected people as quickly and transparently as possible, he added.
The government had announced ₹10,000 each for families whose houses were inundated, irrespective of whether they had stayed in relief camps.
It had also announced rental assistance for families forced to move out of their flooded homes and ₹300 a day for two members of such families.
Commercial establishments damaged by floodwaters were also promised ₹10,000.
The Minister’s assurance comes in the wake of reports that the assistance promised by the government remained on paper even after Onam.
There were also reports that the daily assistance of ₹300 and the relief announced for affected business establishments were yet to reach beneficiaries.
Mr. Anil Kumar said a permanent mechanism would be put in place in the district to deal with monsoon-related disasters.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks lawyers to move Delhi HC for probe into attack on peaceful protest in BCI premises
stories.title: Supreme Court asks lawyers to move Delhi HC for probe into attack on peaceful protest in BCI premises
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked the counsel representing petitioners Kunal Yadav and others, to approach the High Court with their plea that they were physically assaulted, dragged, abused and forcibly thrown out of the BCI office
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 3, 2026) allowed young lawyers to move the Delhi High Court with their petition for an independent investigation into allegations of targeted violence committed against them by an unidentified mob while they were peacefully protesting at the Bar Council of India (BCI) premises on August 21.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked advocate Prashant Bhushan, representing petitioners Kunal Yadav and others, to approach the High Court with their plea that they were physically assaulted, dragged, abused and forcibly thrown out of the BCI premises during a peaceful sit-in for the resignation of chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra and comprehensive reforms in the regulatory body.

“The assault took place inside the BCI premises that are under round-the-clock CCTV surveillance in the presence of a large deployment of Delhi Police personnel, including an officer of the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Police, who did not intervene,” the petition submitted.
Mr. Bhushan, in an oral mentioning, alleged that BCI chairperson, senior advocate Manan Kumar Mishra, had later on referred to the protesting lawyers as “legal cockroaches” who were dealt with.
Mr. Bhushan sought a CBI probe into the affair.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench, said though lawyers have a right to protest, the legal fraternity was still a disciplined community, which had multiple fora to present their grievances.
Mr. Bhushan said nobody had a right to beat up anyone.
The protesting lawyers were mostly in their twenties, he said.
The senior lawyer said he would comply with whatever the top court thought best.
He explained that the petition was filed directly in the Supreme Court as several pleas connected to the BCI were currently being heard by the court.
Chief Justice Kant observed that it would be more opportune if the petition came up before the High Court first.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks NHAI to consider setting up CCTVs, monitoring rooms at toll plazas
stories.title: Supreme Court asks NHAI to consider setting up CCTVs, monitoring rooms at toll plazas
stories.summary: The court was hearing a suo motu case initiated in the wake of two fatal road accidents in November 2025 in Phalodi district of Rajasthan and Rangareddy district of Telangana, which together claimed 34 lives
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 3, 2026) raised concerns over encroachments and stationary vehicles on highways and asked the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) to consider setting up camera surveillance systems and monitoring rooms at toll plazas to address such hazards.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was hearing a suo motu case initiated in the wake of two fatal road accidents in November 2025 in Phalodi district of Rajasthan and Rangareddy district of Telangana, which together claimed 34 lives.

In April, the top court, while issuing a slew of directions had held that the safety of highway users forms an integral part of the right to life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution, and that the State has a positive obligation to prevent avoidable deaths caused by hazards such as illegal parking and accident-prone “blackspots”.
The counsel for the NHAI told the Bench that circulars had been issued requiring regular inspections and highway patrols to curb unauthorised parking.
The Bench, however, suggested the use of technology for more effective monitoring.
“Why can’t you think of having a camera surveillance system?
You can have monitoring rooms at all toll plazas,” the Bench said.
Senior advocate A.N.S. Nadkarni, assisting the court as amicus curiae, said vehicles parked illegally along highways remained a major safety concern and were a recurring cause of road accidents.

During the hearing, the Bench was also informed that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Tamil Nadu government were yet to file their compliance affidavits.
The court granted two weeks for the two Ministries to file their affidavits and directed the Tamil Nadu government to place its response on record before the next hearing.
The matter will be heard next on October 6.
In April, the top court had directed district magistrates to ensure the removal or demolition of all existing and newly detected unauthorised structures within highway safety zones within 60 days.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rules that BCI has no power to punish law students
stories.title: Supreme Court rules that BCI has no power to punish law students
stories.summary: Top court says only the universities they are enrolled in can take action; it rebukes BCI’s attempt to intimidate NALSAR students who opposed inviting CJI Kant as chief guest for their convocation
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 3, 2026) declared that the Bar Council of India (BCI) and its chairperson, Manan Kumar Mishra, lack jurisdiction to discipline or penalise law students, rebuking the regulatory body’s attempts to intimidate NALSAR students exercising their constitutional right to protest.

The court insisted on clarifying the limits of BCI’s powers even though the latter had revoked its August 13 letters to NALSAR administration to launch an inquiry against the students and to the State Bar Councils to block their professional enrolment.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the order, drawing the boundary for BCI, was designed to safeguard university space and students’ right to freely express dissent against future attempts to breach.
“The BCI has no jurisdiction or statutory competence as regards students.
That is for their universities,” Chief Justice Kant observed.

“On an in-depth consideration of the issue, we are of the opinion that the Advocates Act, 1961, does not confer, expressly or impliedly, any power on the Bar Council of India and State Bar Councils to take any disciplinary or punitive action against law students,” the court recorded in the order.
Mr. Mishra, who was present, said the BCI had a role in regulating legal education.
But the court said the BCI could step in only after enrolment.
Its disciplinary powers under the Advocates Act, 1961, were, obviously, limited to registered advocates.
“Till then, BCI did not come into the picture… To say a student will not be enrolled…” Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, leaving the sentence unfinished.

The court was hearing a petition filed by two former NALSAR graduates, represented by senior advocate K. Parameshwar and advocate Rupali Samuel, seeking legal action against the BCI and the chairperson for threatening the 2026 batch of NALSAR students.
The students were protesting against having the CJI as chief guest for their convocation following his oral comments in court comparing youths to ‘cockroaches’ and ‘parasites’.
